statement: In people diagnosed with eye damage after using poppers (113 people in 32 published reports, 2004 to 2021, pooled in a systematic review), evidence is insufficient to say whether stopping poppers, or taking lutein supplements, compared with continuing or not taking them, helps vision recover: treatment was documented for 45 people, of whom 42 were advised to stop (3 of them also given lutein) and 2 were given lutein alone; whether people really stopped was recorded for 27 (19 had); there was no comparison group, and the review states that the effect of treatment or of stopping on vision could not be analysed. Scans improved in most of those followed up (46 of 75), but this cannot be tied to stopping: of the two people followed longest, one who reportedly kept using had unchanged vision and one whose stopping was not recorded improved, and some earlier series saw no improvement in the first months despite stopping. Certainty: very low. Status: single study.
plain: Most people with this eye damage were told to stop using poppers, and a few were given lutein, a supplement, but nobody compared them with people who did not stop, so we do not know whether stopping or lutein helps the eyes recover. Many got better over time either way, as far as the reports show.
population: People diagnosed with eye damage after poppers use (113 published cases, 2004 to 2021)
exposure: Stopping poppers use, or oral lutein
comparator: Continuing use, or no lutein (no comparison group in the reports)
outcome: Recovery of vision and of retinal findings
magnitude: No comparative data. Stopping advised for 42 of the 45 with treatment documented; lutein for 5 (3 with stopping, 2 alone); compliance recorded for 27 (19 compliant); OCT improved or resolved in 46 of 75 followed up, without data by stopping.

evidence.extracted: Treatment documented for 45 patients (39.8%): stopping poppers advised for 42 (93%), 3 of whom also received oral lutein; oral lutein alone for 2; vitrectomy for 1. Compliance documented for 27, of whom 19 (70.3%) were compliant at follow-up.

evidence.extracted: Of the 9 best eyes at 0.4 logMAR or worse, only 2 were followed up and were unchanged; the authors state that it was therefore not possible to analyse the effectiveness of treatment, or of stopping poppers, on acuity.

evidence.locator: Discussion › Visual Acuity, 2nd paragraph; Discussion › Prognosis, 1st paragraph
evidence.extracted: Patient A, reported as not stopping, had acuity 0.2 in both eyes at presentation and at 40-42 months; patient B improved from 0.2 and 0.5 to −0.1 at 46-48 months with no mention of stopping, which the authors take as a sign that patient B had stopped. Some earlier reports found no improvement in acuity and no resolution of foveal damage within 3 months of presentation despite stopping.

evidence.extracted: Of 75 with follow-up OCT, 46 (61.3%) improved or resolved; by time after presentation, 10 of 19 at 1-2 months and 9 of 13 at 3-6 months; results are not given by whether people stopped.

risk_of_bias.note: No comparison group; whether people stopped was recorded for 27 of 113; the authors infer stopping from improvement in one case.

inconsistency.note: The two longest follow-ups and earlier series point in different directions, but there is no comparative estimate to be inconsistent.

imprecision.note: No comparative data; lutein given to 5 people.

grade.reasoning: Observational case data start low; risk of bias -1 and imprecision -1 give very low. Stopping poppers and lutein are what people with this diagnosis were told to do, but no report compared them with not doing so; the improvement seen in many followed-up cases may be the natural course. The claim states findings only (section 7).
